Answers below.

**h01** — `s3presign.Runner` (S3 pre-signed URL refresher) — every 12 h ticker (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`; `Run` loop `:29-41`, `RunOnce`→`CheckAndPresign` `:43-45`), re-signing any S3 attachment whose presigned URL is within 4 days of its 5-day expiry (`runner.go:85-89`) — wired in `server/server.go:162-171` (`startBackgroundRunners`: one immediate `RunOnce(ctx)` at `server/server.go:163`, then the goroutine `Run` at `server/server.go:169`), which `Server.Start` calls at `server/server.go:126`.

**h02** — Delivery function: `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (actual HTTP send at `:152` via the shared `safeClient`); async path enqueues through `webhook.PostAsync` (`:184`) into `asyncPostQueue` drained by 4 goroutines started in `init()` (`:39-55`).
Protection: the client's `Transport.DialContext` is `safeDialContext` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:32-37, 59-77` — which resolves the host and rejects any resolved IP in a reserved/private range (also defeating DNS-rebinding), using `isReservedIP`/`reservedCIDRs` in `internal/webhook/validate.go:14-54`. Secondary, at configuration time: `webhook.ValidateURL` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:62`) called from `server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74,161,182`. Escape hatch: `webhook.AllowPrivateIPs` (`validate.go:41`), set from `--allow-private-webhooks` at `cmd/memos/main.go:49`.

**h03** — Abstraction package: `internal/idp` (`internal/idp/idp.go:3-8`, `IdentityProviderUserInfo`); concrete implementation: `internal/idp/oauth2` (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:20-107` — `IdentityProvider`, `NewIdentityProvider`, `ExchangeToken`, `UserInfo`). OAuth2 is the only protocol implementation that ships.

**h04** — No. `mysql.NewDB` is referenced exactly once in the entire repo, inside the factory: `store/db/db.go:22` (switch on `profile.Driver`, `store/db/db.go:18-27`). Evidence: `grep -rn "mysql.NewDB\|&mysql.DB{" --include=*.go .` returns only that line; the only file importing `store/db/mysql` is `store/db/db.go`; `NewDB` (`store/db/mysql/mysql.go:20`) is the package's sole constructor and `DB` (`:14`) is never composite-literal-constructed elsewhere. `store/test/containers.go:101-105` uses the testcontainers MySQL module, not this driver type.

**h05** — Explicit Go code (no DB-level cascade). Deleted in the same transaction as the user, in each driver's `DeleteUser`: reactions *on the user's memos* via `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx` and reactions *created by the user* via `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` — `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:96,102` (impls `:380-403`), `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:96,102` (impls `:380-403`), `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:96,102` (impls `:417-440`); orchestrated by `deleteUserTargetsTx` (`store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:92-127`) called from `DeleteUser` (`:29-59`), invoked by `Store.DeleteUser` (`store/user.go:171-181`).
What I checked to rule out a DB rule: `reaction` table has no foreign keys in any dialect — `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:92-99`, `store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql:91-98`, mysql LATEST equivalent; a repo-wide grep for `ON DELETE`/`REFERENCES` under `store/migration/` shows cascades only for `memo_share.memo_id` (`store/migration/*/LATEST.sql:108-109`) and legacy sqlite ≤0.5 tables, never `reaction`.

**h06** — Handlers (all `*APIV1Service`):
- `CreateMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:70` → `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` at `:157`
- `UpdateMemo` — `memo_service.go:401` → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` at `:513`
- `DeleteMemo` — `memo_service.go:518` → `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` at `:562`
- `CreateMemoComment` — `memo_service_comments.go:20` → `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` at `:119`
- `SetMemoAttachments` — `memo_attachment_service.go:16` → `:48`

Convergence function: `webhook.PostAsync` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:184` (every path reaches it via `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:48-74` or `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` `:30-46`); it queues to `webhook.Post` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`), which performs the request.

**h07** — Browser hits `/file/users/{identifier}/avatar` (URL produced at `server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:36`):
- route registration — `fileGroup.GET("/users/:identifier/avatar", s.serveUserAvatar)` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124`
- `(*FileServerService).serveUserAvatar` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168`
- `(*FileServerService).getUserByUsername` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715`
- `(*store.Store).GetUser` — `store/user.go:148` (userCache is consulted only for ID lookups, `:149-156`, so a username lookup always falls through)
- `(*store.Store).ListUsers` — `store/user.go:136` → `s.driver.ListUsers`
- `store.Driver.ListUsers` (interface) — `store/driver.go:46`
- `(*sqlite.DB).ListUsers` — `store/db/sqlite/user.go:88` (SELECT includes `avatar_url`, `:159,189`); mysql/postgres equivalents behind the same interface
- back in the handler: `parseDataURI` (`fileserver.go:737`) decodes the base64 data URI in `user.AvatarURL` and it is blobbed out at `fileserver.go:207`.

**h08** — Two declarers:
- `(*s3presign.Runner).RunOnce` — `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:43` — yes, invoked from production — callers: `server/server.go:163` (`startBackgroundRunners`) and `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:36` (its own ticker loop).
- `(*memopayload.Runner).RunOnce` — `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27` — no — not invoked anywhere (no production or test caller; only the package-level helper `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` is used, from `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108,447`). `Runner`/`NewRunner` (`memopayload/runner.go:14,19`) are likewise never constructed.

**h09** — Count: 8 declarations of a method named `Close` in backend Go — 6 concrete methods plus 2 interface declarations; (10 if the two test-only helpers are counted).
- Concrete: `(*store.Store).Close` `store/store.go:72`; `(*sqlite.DB).Close` `store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:67`; `(*mysql.DB).Close` `store/db/mysql/mysql.go:47`; `(*postgres.DB).Close` `store/db/postgres/postgres.go:46`; `(*cache.Cache).Close` `store/cache/cache.go:187`; `(*apiv1.SSEHub).Close` `server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:99`
- Interface: `store.Driver.Close` `store/driver.go:12`; `cache.Interface.Close` `store/cache/cache.go:30`
- Test-only: `store/test/filter_helpers_test.go:200,282`

Invoked by non-test server code:
- `(*store.Store).Close` — caller `server/server.go:146` (`Server.Shutdown`)
- `(*apiv1.SSEHub).Close` — caller `server/server.go:206` (`closeLongLivedConnections`)
- `(*cache.Cache).Close` ×3 — caller `store/store.go:74-76`
- `store.Driver.Close` → the concrete `(*sqlite|*mysql|*postgres).DB.Close` — caller `store/store.go:78` (sqlite in a default install)

**h10** — `(*filter.Engine).CompileToStatement` — `internal/filter/engine.go:74` — ~38 call sites (7 non-test: `internal/filter/helpers.go:11`, `store/db/sqlite/memo_relation.go:85`, `store/db/postgres/memo_relation.go:87,98`, `store/db/mysql/memo_relation.go:78`, `server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go:356`, `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:413`; the rest in `internal/filter/*_test.go`). Runners-up: `filter.NewEngine` (`internal/filter/engine.go:24`, ~33), `(*renderer).addArg` (`internal/filter/render.go:842`, 28 — highest if counting production code only), `util.GenUUID` (`internal/util/util.go:40`, 28 total / 7 production). Note `internal/filter/helpers.go:9 AppendConditions` funnels most store-layer filter queries into `CompileToStatement`.

**h11** — 1st: `store.User` (`store/user.go:40`) — referenced from ~7 packages outside `store/` (`server/auth`, `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/fileserver`, `server/router/frontend`, `server/router/rss`; ~99 references). 2nd: `store.Memo` (`store/memo.go:12`) — ~6 packages (`server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/frontend`, `server/router/rss`, `server/runner/memopayload`; ~73 references). (`store.Attachment` is third at ~4 packages.)

**h12** — Concrete method: `(*sqlite.DB).CreateMemo` — `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:16` (the `INSERT INTO \`memo\` … RETURNING` at `:41-42`).
Determination: the driver is selected at runtime by `db.NewDBDriver` switching on `profile.Driver` (`store/db/db.go:18-27`); the default value of that field is `"sqlite"` — `viper.SetDefault("driver", "sqlite")` at `cmd/memos/main.go:122` and the flag default at `cmd/memos/main.go:130`, read into the profile at `cmd/memos/main.go:43`. So with no flags the `store.Driver` interface value (`store/driver.go:10,29`) is `*sqlite.DB`. Call chain: `APIV1Service.CreateMemo` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:70`) → `Store.CreateMemo` (`store/memo.go:109-114`) → `s.driver.CreateMemo` → the sqlite method. (mysql/postgres `CreateMemo` are the other candidates, reachable only with `--driver mysql|postgres`.)

**h13** — Implementation: the unexported `*markdown.service` — `internal/markdown/markdown.go:58-60` — the only type implementing `markdown.Service` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:31-56`); no mocks/fakes exist.
Construction: `markdown.NewService(...)` — `internal/markdown/markdown.go:85-111` — called in production exactly once, in `NewAPIV1Service` with `WithTagExtension()` + `WithMentionExtension()` — `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48-51` (plus the test helper `server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:44`).
Holders of the interface: `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35`); `RSSService.MarkdownService` (`server/router/rss/rss.go:45`, injected from the API service at `server/server.go:85`); `memopayload.Runner.MarkdownService` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16`) and the `markdown.Service` parameter of `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`).

**h14** — Computation site: `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` — `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74-88` — which delegates to `(*markdown.service).ExtractAll` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go`, tags via `ExtractTags` `:142`, properties via `ExtractProperties` `:190`) and writes `memo.Payload.Tags` / `memo.Payload.Property` (`runner.go:85-86`).
Triggers: memo creation — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` (in `CreateMemo`, hence also `CreateMemoComment` which routes through it); memo update when the `content` field is in the update mask — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447` (in `UpdateMemo`); plus the bulk rebuilder `(*memopayload.Runner).RunOnce` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27`), which is currently not wired to any caller.
Extracted properties: `tags` (deduplicated `#tag` nodes, excluding tags inside links/images) and `MemoPayload.Property` = `has_link`, `has_task_list`, `has_code`, `has_incomplete_tasks`, `title` (text of a leading H1) — `internal/markdown/markdown.go:190-232`, `proto/store/memo.proto:12-22`. (Location is set separately by the user, `memo_service.go:112-114`.)

- `(*APIV1Service).checkMemoReadAccess` (per-memo read gate for `GetMemo`/comment listing) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:39-68` (callers `:356`, `:367`, `memo_service_comments.go:148`)

- Mention/notification fan-out — `server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:62-84`, `server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go:309-312`, `server/notification/email.go:313-316`

**r01** — False premise: there is no Redis and no Redis configuration anywhere in the repo (`grep -rni redis` over Go/mod/config files returns nothing; `go.mod` has no Redis client). The cache layer is a process-local in-memory cache: `store/cache/cache.go` (`Cache` backed by `sync.Map`, `:65-71`; `New` starts a cleanup goroutine `:73-83`). Three caches are created in `store.New` — `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` — with `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`, `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute`, `MaxItems: 1000` (`store/store.go:38-51`; identical `cache.DefaultConfig` at `store/cache/cache.go:56-63`). So user entries expire after **10 minutes**, set via `Set`→`SetWithTTL` (`store/cache/cache.go:89-118`) from `store/user.go:143,167`, and are invalidated explicitly on update/delete (`store/user_delete.go:39-47`).

**r02** — False premise: there is no per-user API rate-limiting middleware and no request limits. Nothing in the repo imports a limiter (`golang.org/x/time/rate` is absent from `go.mod`); the only match for "rate limit" is an aspirational comment in `internal/email/doc.go:86`. The full middleware stack is `middleware.Recover()` and the CORS middleware (`server/server.go:51-52`, `server/cors.go:14`), plus static/SPA middleware for the frontend (`server/router/frontend/frontend.go:54,59`) and the auth interceptor/authorizer on the gRPC-Gateway & Connect paths (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:64-100`). What does exist are non-rate-limit concurrency bounds: semaphores for thumbnail/image work (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:60-61`, `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:106,114`) and the 128-slot webhook dispatch queue (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`).

**r03** — False premise: there is no cron scheduler running and no nightly database-cleanup job. `internal/scheduler` is a standalone, unused cron library — outside its own package and tests, nothing references it (`grep -rn "scheduler\." --exclude=*_test.go` yields only files inside `internal/scheduler/`); no `scheduler.New()`/`Register()` call exists in `cmd/` or `server/`. The `"0 2 * * *" // 2 AM daily` "daily-cleanup" is only a documentation example (`internal/scheduler/doc.go:14-21`, `internal/scheduler/README.md`). The only real periodic work is the 12-hour S3 presign runner (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`, wired at `server/server.go:162-171`) and each cache's 5-minute expiry sweep (`store/cache/cache.go:218`, config at `store/store.go:40`).

**r04** — False premise: neither — there is no message broker at all (no NATS, RabbitMQ, or AMQP dependency in `go.mod`; no queue is declared anywhere). Webhook delivery is in-process: a buffered Go channel `asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`) drained by 4 worker goroutines started in `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`), fed by `PostAsync` (`:184-196`, which drops the payload and logs a warning when the buffer is full) and delivered by `Post` (`:120-180`). Consequences: the queue is not durable — pending webhooks are lost on restart, and there are no retries.

**r05** — False premise: there is no GraphQL schema, server, or dependency anywhere in the repo (no `graphql` match in Go sources or `go.mod`). The public API surface is protobuf-defined and served three ways from `server/router/api/v1`: Connect/gRPC handlers and a gRPC-Gateway REST/JSON transcoding layer registered by `APIV1Service.RegisterGateway` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:64+`, schemas in `proto/api/v1/*.proto`, generated code in `proto/gen/api/v1/`), plus SSE for live events (`server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`). Alongside it: an HTTP file server (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:122-125`), RSS feeds (`server/router/rss/rss.go`), an MCP endpoint (`server/router/mcp/service.go`, registered `server/server.go:88-93`), and `/healthz` (`server/server.go:64`). An OpenAPI description is generated for MCP at `server/router/mcp/openapi.go`.
